about: A Zork-style underground adventure, a final test set by a silver-haired old man. You explore caverns and a shadowy land by a cliff and sea, and a hooded swordsman duels you.

done.why: I had escaped the duel and seen a handful of rooms. The combat felt opaque and I had smashed my own lamp, so I stopped.

moments.note: Shouting summoned a hooded swordsman and a glowing sword appeared in my hand.
Attacking repeatedly gave 'ignores your feeble attack' and I could not tell how to win.
Throwing the lamp smashed it and left me in the dark, still being dueled.
Going down the cliff path ended the duel; the sword stopped glowing.

wished: Know how to actually win or end the duel
Parse natural phrasing like 'ask the lantern' or 'parry'
A warning before destroying my only light

lines.line: Who do you think you are? Arthur?
lines.why: A playful reply to my pulling the sword from the rock.

lines.line: From nowhere, the sword from the junction appears in your hand, wildly glowing!
lines.why: A surprising trigger from just shouting.

lines.line: Although you are defenseless, the figure reaches for your sword and hands it back to you, nodding grimly.
lines.why: It shows the fight is a test, not a killing.

fun.why: Charming surprises, but the duel was opaque.

engagement.why: The mystery of the duel held me for a while.

difficulty.why: I never found how to progress in the fight.

interestingness.why: A sparring test with a gentle tone is an interesting idea.

prose.why: Evocative room descriptions and a good dream opening.
